title: Cluster 01 DRILL: Terms, Monohybrid Crosses and Sex Linkage
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 6 · 11 questions · 83 marks · 36 parts · one mark per minute, so a little under an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question.

Book 6 is procedural, and that changes what this drill is. Most of the marks in this Book come from executing a genetic diagram to a fixed layout, not from explaining a mechanism. On the 9477 specimen, eight of the eleven Book 6 marks on Paper 2 were procedural. So the schemes below pay you row by row: the allele key, the parental phenotypes, the parental genotypes, the circled gametes, the offspring genotypes, the offspring phenotypes, the ratio. Write every row every time, even when you can see the answer without one. Two mistakes in one row scores zero for that row.

Four real pedigree figures, three questions figure-led. Sex linkage and pedigree analysis is the largest single concept in Book 6 at 246 of the 1000 curated records, and it is 76% figure-led. There is no way to prepare for it by reading. Every figure is the real image from the paper it came from, not a redrawing.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then asks you to justify every option, which is where the four choices get checked instead of eliminated by feel.

Question 4 is the full-cycle question. SAJC Prelim 2023 Paper 2 Question 5 end to end, all four parts at their real 8 marks: name the mode of inheritance, justify it, lay out the whole diagram, then read a probability off your own square.

Cumulative over Books 2 and 3. Q2(b) needs gene mutation from Book 2 as the only source of a new allele. Q3 needs crossing over, independent assortment at metaphase I and random fertilisation said cold from Book 3. Q5(b) needs frameshift and nonsense mutation from Book 2. A Book 2 or Book 3 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 1 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Define every term inside the question's own situation, because two examiner comments in this file punish the abstract version. Keep gene and allele apart in both directions; an organism is homozygous, alleles are identical. Circle your gametes. Put every genotype under its phenotype. State sex as well as trait on the phenotype row of any sex-linked diagram. On a pedigree, give the conclusion and the feature that forces it, because a scheme rejects the conclusion on its own.

One warning about your own notes, and it sits inside Question 7. Chapter 6.1 page 31 introduces Fig. 16 as showing sex-linked recessive inheritance while the section heading, the caption, the genotypes inside the figure and the characteristics list all say dominant. The caption is right and the lead-in sentence is wrong. Question 7 is an X-linked dominant pedigree and Question 6 marking point 4 is the observation that rules X-linked dominance out. Get those two the wrong way round and both questions collapse.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as for duplicated labels. Q1 the ten terms said inside the question's own situation · Q2 the five-link chain from allele to trait · Q3 how one allele of each pair reaches a gamete, and how a cross is kept clean · Q4 a whole sex-linked cross end to end · Q5 what changes when the heterozygote is not simply dominant · Q6 proving autosomal dominance from a family, including the observation that kills X-linked dominance · Q7 an X-linked dominant family, then the diagram that comes out of it · Q8 dominance explained at the level of the enzyme, then X-linked recessive evidence · Q9 finding out where a gene sits by swapping the sexes · Q10 counting gamete types · Q11 more than two alleles in a population, two in an individual. The three pedigree questions require three different answers: Q6 wants autosomal dominant justified through rarity, heterozygosity and an unaffected daughter of an affected father; Q7 wants X-linked dominant justified through all-daughters-affected with a named example; Q8 wants X-linked recessive justified through the sons of an affected mother. The four genetic diagrams also differ: Q4(c) is X-linked recessive from a carrier mother, Q5(a) is autosomal codominance, Q7(b) is X-linked dominant from an affected father, Q9(b) is reverse-engineered from an offspring table.

Nothing from Books 7 to 9, and no two-gene crosses. Dihybrid crosses, test crosses, autosomal linkage and epistasis are Cluster 2, so every cross in this drill turns on one gene. The word epistasis is used once, in Q11(e), only as the thing the data points to.
